common_datasets: Model-generated prompts by few-shot prompting a pre-trained model (140,335)
Human feedback data for preference model comparisons (collected in prior work)
Helpfulness and harmlessness data collected separately by crowdworkers
Dataset from [Ganguli et al., 2022] for harm-focused multiple choice evaluations
Survey of 399 undergraduate and postgraduate students from various disciplines in Hong Kong.
common_algorithms: Fine-tuning a pretrained language model on revised responses (Supervised Learning)
Training a preference model from AI preferences
Reinforcement learning using the preference model as a reward signal (RLAIF)
common_key_findings: Constitutional AI can train a harmless but non-evasive AI assistant without human labels for harmfulness.
The AI feedback (RLAIF) approach can train models that are preferred by crowdworkers over models trained with human feedback for harmlessness.
Chain-of-thought reasoning improves AI's ability to identify harms and leads to evaluations competitive with human feedback-trained preference models.
Model-generated critiques and revisions can progressively reduce harmfulness.
Generating critiques improves harmlessness compared to directly generating revisions.
Self-supervised preference labels for RL further improve model behavior, equaling or exceeding performance with human feedback for harmlessness.
Increasing the number of principles in the constitution does not significantly improve harmlessness scores but can improve response diversity.
Critiqued revisions generally achieve higher harmlessness scores than direct revisions, especially for smaller models.
RLAIF models are significantly more harmless than RLHF and SL-CAI models, with minimal cost to helpfulness.
RL-CAI models are virtually never evasive and often give nuanced and harmless responses to red team prompts.
